public_rationale: An enforceable FCC compliance plan addressing the transmission of AI-generated political deception was active when Marcus wrote. That is sufficient to contradict absolutely nothing, even within the narrower federal scope. It does not show that the overall response was adequate or that medical misinformation was addressed.
limitations: The measure targets caller authentication and transmission practices, not every form of misinformation.
The publication-day status follows from the decree's continuing term; it is not a separately reported May 16 action.
The evidence establishes legal obligations, not their effectiveness or full compliance.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nothing is being done about political or medical AI-generated misinformation.

statement.excerpt: Absolutely nothing is being done about AI-generated misinformation, political or medical.
statement.document_title: Two Years Ago Today in AI History: The Tale of An About-face in AI Regulation

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that no concrete governmental action addressing either category was active at publication.
The surrounding Washington discussion makes federal action the strongest test; a federal counterexample avoids dependence on a broader state or private-sector reading.
An enforceable, continuing compliance obligation directed at AI-generated political deception counts as action. The claim does not require proof that the action solved the problem.
The target is the publication-day state because ongoing legal obligations have no quarterly reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive review establishes that no relevant governmental rule, enforcement measure or operational program was active on May 16, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one concrete federal measure addressing AI-generated political or medical misinformation was active on May 16, 2025.

evidence.locator: Adopting Order paragraph 1; Consent Decree paragraphs 2(h), 17–20 and Attachment 1
evidence.explanation: The decree responded to calls using a cloned Biden voice to discourage primary voting and imposed continuing verification, training and reporting duties. Its August 2024 effective date and 36-month term place those duties in force on May 16, 2025; the event date describes that continuing legal obligation, not a new enforcement action.
